result_text:
The per-rep purchase order count now leaves out cancelled purchase orders, so the example from the task gives Anna 2 and Bob 1.

**Change:** `src/main/java/com/acme/backoffice/PurchaseOrderStore.java`, in `countPerSalesRep` (around line 298). The count subquery had no status filter. I added the existing `NOT_CANCELLED` condition, the same one the per-quarter and weekday counts use. Reps with no orders in the period still appear with 0, and the ordering is unchanged.

**Test:** `src/test/java/com/acme/backoffice/SalesRepPurchaseOrderCountTest.java` has a new `cancelledPurchaseOrdersAreNotCounted` case. It has three sent orders and one cancelled order into the South warehouse, and it expects `Bob:3, Anna:1`. The first run failed only because I had written the expected list in the wrong order. After fixing that, I ran the per-rep test class and the other purchase-order tests with `mvn -q -o`. They passed with no output. I didn't check the exit code explicitly.

Nothing is committed. I left `countPerCountry` alone, since the task only covers the per-rep report, but it has the same gap: it doesn't filter cancelled orders either.
